metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust downward; force mean reversion toward recent 7-day average if sentiment shifts >0.5.
- Model underestimates prices when sentiment is mixed or weakly positive; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment >0.3 for 3+ consecutive days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the forecast window; apply 1–3% downward correction for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a spike, model fails to reflect this; use 14-day moving average as anchor for correction if price deviates >10% from prior 14-day range.
